I have farmed this soil for decades and it is weak, so I will spread some cow dung and a small amount of the government NPK fertilizer to help the sorghum grow. I always keep seed from my last harvest because the improved seeds from the agro-dealer are too costly and hard to find, and on a plot this small my children and I can manage all the weeding and harvesting by hand. We depend entirely on the June rains because there is no irrigation water here, and sorghum does not need spraying like vegetables, so I will not buy chemicals.
